blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — Residents in parts of Samar and Eastern Samar have been warned against gathering and consuming shellfish after red tide toxins were detected in several coastal waters, as the shellfish ban remains in effect in three major bays in the region. The Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) reported on Friday that seawater samples collected from Daram Island, Samar, tested positive for Pyrodinium bahamense, a toxin-producing microorganism associated with paralytic shellfish poisoning.
